transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start off, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in today?

Well... my wife told me I should come. She thinks I'm worrying too much. But... I don't know. I just... I hear things. When I'm playing dominoes with the men, they say things. Just little messages, you know? Meant for me. And sometimes the man on the radio does it too. My wife says it's just regular talk, but... I know they're warning me. Telling me to be careful.
Have you been using any alcohol, drugs, or other substances recently—like marijuana, stimulants, or anything else?
No. I don't... I don't use any of that. Just my regular medicine for my heart, that's all. I don't drink. Never cared for it.

Besides these experiences, have you noticed any big changes in your mood lately—like feeling very sad, hopeless, or on the other hand, unusually energetic, elated, or needing much less sleep than usual?

Well... I suppose there are times. Sometimes I wake up feeling... very good. Bright, I guess. Like I have important things to do. I might talk a bit faster then, maybe laugh more. But... if my wife or someone tries to slow me down, or asks too many questions about what I'm doing... I don't like it. I get a bit sharp with them. That's all.

When you're not feeling unusually 'bright' or energetic—during your regular, normal mood days—do you still hear those messages from the men or the radio, or does that only happen during the times you feel especially good?

Well... yes. Even when I'm just... regular. A while back, there was a whole month. I was sleeping fine, not doing anything special. Just normal days. But... I still heard them. My friend on the porch. And the radio, still talking to me. It doesn't just stop when I'm feeling quiet.

Thinking back over the whole time you've been hearing these messages, would you say the 'bright,' high-energy periods have made up a large portion of that time, or have they been brief and infrequent compared to your normal days?

Well... I suppose... if you look at the whole time since this all began... 

It's mostly been those... bright times. The energetic spells. And then the time it takes to settle down after. 

Most of the months have been like that, I guess. More of that than the quiet days.
About how long ago did all of this begin—hearing the messages and having these bright, energetic spells—from the very start until now?
Well... I suppose it's been... about a year and a half. A year and five months, maybe. It started... well, after my friend passed away. That's when it began.

This pattern fits schizoaffective disorder (bipolar type) better than schizophrenia, so F20.0 is ruled out.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports continuous psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations attributing personal messages to others, delusions of reference) that have persisted for at least a month during a period of stable, non-elevated mood, confirming psychosis independent of mood disturbance. However, he also describes recurrent manic-like episodes (elevated/'bright' mood, increased energy, rapid speech, decreased need for concern about sleep, irritability when questioned) that, by his own account, have constituted the majority of the total illness duration (~1.5 years). This combination—mood episode symptoms present for the majority of the illness duration plus psychotic symptoms persisting for ≥2 weeks in the absence of mood symptoms—meets criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type (F25.0) rather than pure Bipolar Disorder (mood symptoms alone would not explain persistent psychosis in euthymic periods) or Schizophrenia (mood episodes are prominent and occupy a substantial portion of the illness course, not just a brief superimposed period).
